title: Capacity-tag mismatch caused private deployment to swap to incompatible quantized variant
creator: Aisha Patel
description: A customer (EduTech Inc.) reported repeated model failures and semantic regressions from their private deployment after a routine capacity tag update. Investigation shows the control plane incorrectly matched a node's capacity tag to a quantized variant (int4) incompatible with the pinned model variant, causing the serving runtime to swap to a lower-precision artifact and produce malformed logits and higher downstream error rates. This produced 5xx errors for some requests and degraded answer quality for others. Issue surfaced after capacity tagging update during a Private upgrade window.
impact_summary: Approximately 12% of requests to the customer's private cluster saw either 5xx errors or outputs with severe quality regressions over a 3-hour window. Customer SLA was breached; they opened an escalation with Support and requested urgent rollback and RCA. Scope appears limited to Private deployments using capacity tags + quantized model catalog entries, but similar selector logic exists in Dedicated routing and could be affected under specific rollouts.
repro_steps: 1) Deploy a private cluster with a pinned model version that has both float16 and int4 variants registered in catalog.
2) Apply a capacity tag update that changes node metadata to include legacy-capacity:low-int4 (simulating operator script used by customer).
3) Trigger routing policy refresh (policy sync) on control plane or wait for TTL to expire.
4) Send normal inference traffic; observe that some requests are routed to the int4 variant even though tenant model pinning should prevent variant swaps.
5) Confirm increased 5xx errors and degraded response quality compared to pre-update baseline.
root_cause: A logic error in the policy merge function inadvertently treated capacity-tag keys with suffixes (e.g., 'low-int4') as higher-priority selectors than explicit tenant model pins when computing compatible variants. The merge order puts node capability-derived selectors ahead of tenant pins during partial policy refreshes, allowing the runtime to select a quantized variant incompatible with the pinned architecture. Additionally, a missing compatibility check between model binary metadata and runtime decoder led to 5xxs instead of graceful fallbacks.
mitigation: Rolled back the customer's capacity tag changes and force-synced policies to restore previous routing. We implemented a temporary guard in the control plane to ignore capacity-tag selectors when a tenant has an explicit model pin. Customer cluster returned to normal within 22 minutes after rollback. SLA credit and incident summary provided to customer.
resolution: Code fix merged: reorder policy merge priorities so tenant pins are always honored above node-derived selectors; add explicit compatibility checks rejecting incompatible quantized artifacts with clear metric/emitter for rejection. Added unit tests and an integration test that simulates capacity-tag updates. Backport applied to runtime-2.3.1. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345. Change will be included in runtime-2.3.2 stable release.

notes: Follow-up: Add a monitoring alert that fires when policy-derived selector utilization deviates >5% from tenant pin expectations for a tenant over 30m.
Follow-up: Improve catalog metadata to include explicit runtime compatibility flags to prevent accidental variant selection.
Follow-up: Create a runbook for private deployment upgrades that lists capacity-tagging as a high-risk step and requires a canary/validation phase.
